Title: Path Trace
Description: Watch packet loss and latency at each hop. ICMP probes leave your computer through the local agent.
Seo_Title: ICMP path trace (MTR) from your computer | MyDevTools
Keywords: path trace, MTR, traceroute, ICMP, hop latency, packet loss, local agent
PrivacyShort: ICMP probes leave your computer through the local agent. Hop results stay on this page.
PairCodeHint: Paste the current code from the agent window. The field is cleared after each attempt.
Disconnected: Disconnected. The trace stopped with the session.
PrivateAllowed: Private and loopback targets are allowed
PrivateBlocked: Private and loopback targets are blocked
ConnectionNotSaved: This browser could not store the connection or the settings. They last only until you leave the page.
SetupIntro: Download and start the local agent, then come back to this page.
SetupStep2: Start MyDevTools Agent. On Linux, ICMP needs the ping group range or CAP_NET_RAW.
SetupStep3: Copy the pairing code from the agent window.
SetupStep4: Paste the code below. If the browser asks for local-network access, allow it for this connection.
PrivateSetupNote: Private, loopback and LAN targets are blocked by default. Restart the agent with --allow-private only when you intentionally need them. Routers seen along a path are shown even when they use a private address. Pairing adds icmp.trace and keeps capabilities already granted in this browser; it never grants a scanner.
PrivacyNote: The browser sends the target and probe settings only to the agent on 127.0.0.1. ICMP probes go from the agent onto the network, so the target and the routers on the path can see this computer. MyDevTools servers do not receive the target or the hop table. This browser remembers recent targets and these settings. It does not store hop results or the pairing code.
NeedTraceCapability: This connection can send HTTP requests, but it cannot trace paths yet. Enter a new pairing code to add path tracing. The saved HTTP session stays until that pairing succeeds.
NotConnected: Connect the local agent before starting a trace.
TargetHint: One host name or IP address. The first resolved address is probed. Routers on the path are shown even when their address is private.
IntervalHint: Milliseconds between probes, from 200 to 60000. The next probe waits out the remainder of the interval. Default 1000.
PayloadHint: ICMP payload size, from 0 to 1472 bytes. Don't Fragment stays on. Default 64.
MaxHopsHint: How many hops to probe, from 1 to 64. Probes stop at the destination. Default 30.
TimeoutHint: How long each probe waits, from 100 to 30000 ms. Default 5000.
EmptyTable: Start a trace to fill the hop table.
InvalidTarget: Enter one host name or IP address, without a URL, a path, or spaces.
InvalidSettings: Check the interval (200–60000 ms), payload (0–1472 bytes), hop limit (1–64) and timeout (100–30000 ms).
Error_agent_unavailable: The local agent is not reachable at 127.0.0.1:48732.
Error_invalid_response: The agent returned a response this page could not read.
Error_invalid_request: The agent rejected the target or the probe settings.
Error_unauthorized: The session is missing or expired. Pair again.
Error_forbidden: This session cannot trace paths. Enter a new pairing code to add path tracing.
Error_pairing_invalid: The pairing code is not valid.
Error_pairing_expired: The pairing code expired. Copy a new one from the agent.
Error_pairing_rate_limited: Too many pairing attempts. Wait and try again.
Error_unsupported_capability: This agent does not advertise path tracing (icmp.trace). Use a build that includes it.
Error_private_network_denied: Private and loopback targets need the agent started with --allow-private.
Error_target_denied: That target is always blocked. Metadata, link-local and multicast addresses cannot be traced.
Error_busy: The agent is already running as many traces as it allows.
Error_network_error: The request to the local agent failed.
Error_incompatible_protocol: This page and the agent use different protocol versions.
Error_name_not_found: That name did not resolve. No probes were sent.

Seo_Introduction: Path Trace sends continuous ICMP echo probes from the MyDevTools local agent on your computer and shows loss and latency at each hop. The browser never sends ICMP itself. The agent grants icmp.trace separately from http.request.
Seo_DetailedDescription: The table updates while the trace runs. Each hop records packets sent and received, loss, and the last, best, average and worst round-trip time, the sample standard deviation, and the average jitter. A silent hop shows “No response” and keeps an empty address. A router answer stays visible, including a home gateway or a CGNAT address in 100.64.0.0/10. Those addresses are observations of the path. They are not new targets. The host you type is checked on its own: private and loopback targets need --allow-private, and metadata, link-local and multicast targets are always refused. Probes stop at the destination or when the same router repeats at the end of the path. Copy or download the current table as text or HTML. The agent does not write that report to disk. Recent targets and the interval, payload size, hop limit, timeout and name-resolution setting stay in this browser. Hop results are not stored.
Seo_Examples:
- `1.1.1.1` traces a public resolver with a 64-byte payload, 30 hops and a 5 second probe timeout.
- `example.com` resolves through the computer's DNS, then probes the first address only.
- `127.0.0.1` needs the agent started with `--allow-private`.
Seo_HowToSteps:
### Step 1: Start the local agent
Download the agent, start it, and copy the pairing code. On Linux, ICMP needs the ping group range or CAP_NET_RAW.

### Step 2: Pair path tracing
Paste the code and connect. The page asks for icmp.trace and keeps capabilities this browser already holds, such as http.request.

### Step 3: Trace a host
Enter one host name or IP address, adjust the interval, payload, hop limit and timeout if you need to, then press Start. Press Stop to finish. The last snapshot stays on the page.

### Step 4: Copy the report
Select a hop to read its ICMP status. Copy or download the table as text or HTML.
Seo_Tips:
- Loss is an integer. Before any probe is sent it is 0. After that it is 100 minus 100 times received divided by sent.
- A missing round-trip time is a dash, not zero.
- Standard deviation and average jitter appear after two replies, in tenths of a millisecond. A timeout is not a sample. Jitter is the running mean of the absolute gap between consecutive replies.
- Turn off name resolution to keep the numeric address in the host column.
- The agent runs at most two traces at once. Each desktop window starts its own trace.
- The published Windows download may be older than this page. Path tracing needs an agent that advertises icmp.trace.
